subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A client tells their paralegal, "I am so broke because of this lawsuit, I am going to rob a convenience store tonight using a replica toy gun to get cash." Can the paralegal disclose this information to the police?
options: Yes, a paralegal can disclose any planned future crime.

No, the exception to confidentiality only applies if there is an imminent risk of death or serious bodily harm; a robbery with a toy gun, while criminal, may not meet this high threshold unless physical harm is intended.
Yes, robbery is an indictable offence and must be reported.
No, the paralegal must wait until the robbery actually happens before reporting.
questions.explain: Rule 3.03 (Confidentiality) provides a very narrow exception for public safety. A paralegal *may* disclose confidential information only if they believe on reasonable grounds that there is an *imminent risk of death or serious bodily harm*. Planned financial crimes or property crimes without risk of serious bodily harm do not trigger this exception.
